When your scene starts, three things happen, one after another. First, the penguin says "Hello" in a speech bubble. Next, it turns left by a quarter of a full spin, so it faces a new way. Last, it moves 2 metres forward, in the direction it's now facing. All three blocks are inside "When the scene starts". Press play to watch them. Can you guess where the penguin will end up?

A do together block makes the blocks inside it all happen at the same time. Usually blocks run one after another. In your scene, the penguin says Hello, then turns, then moves forward. If you put the turn block and the move block inside a do together block, the penguin would turn and move at once, so it would swoop round in a curve. It's great for things like walking and talking together, or two characters moving at the same moment. Why not try it and see what your penguin does?
I explained that a do together block makes the blocks inside it happen at the same time, instead of one after another. I used your penguin as the example and lit up its turn and move blocks. Inside a do together block, those two would happen at once, so the penguin would swoop round in a curve.

Real penguins can't fly, but in your film yours can! The penguin can't flap its wings by itself, so you make it fly with move blocks. In "When the scene starts", add a penguin move block and set it to up, about 2 metres. Then add another move block set to forward, so it zooms along. If you want both to happen at once, put them inside a "do together" block. Give each one a duration, like 2 seconds, so it glides slowly. To land, finish with a move block set to down. Try it and press play!

Duration is how long the turn takes, in seconds. If you leave it out, the turn takes 1 second. If you set duration to 3, your penguin turns slowly, over 3 seconds. If you set it to 0.5, it turns quickly. If you set it to 0, it jumps round straight away. Try changing the duration on your penguin's turn block and press play to see the difference!

Good question! The move block sends the penguin a set way, like forward, left or up, by a number of metres. It doesn't care what's around it. The move toward block sends the penguin toward another thing, like the tree, by a number of metres. So if you want the penguin to head for the tree wherever it is, use move toward. If you just want it to step forward 2 metres, use move.

In "When the scene starts", blocks run one after another, from top to bottom. Each block waits for the one above it to finish. So your penguin says Hello first, then turns, then moves. To make things happen at the same time, use a "do together" block. Drag one into "When the scene starts". Then drag the say block and the turn block inside it. Everything inside "do together" starts at the same moment. Leave the move block underneath if you want the penguin to move after that.

Good question! In StoryStage, models don't bump into each other on their own. The move block just slides your penguin forward 2 metres, and it doesn't know the tree is there. So if the tree is in the way, the penguin goes right through it. To fix it, you could change the turn or move blocks so the penguin's path goes round the tree. Or you could use a "move toward" block and give it a shorter distance, so the penguin stops before it reaches the tree. Try changing the amount in your move block and play the scene to see what happens!

Your penguin's turn block says "left" with amount 0.25. That's a quarter turn to the left. The left is the penguin's own left, not yours. If the penguin is facing you, its left is on your right, so it can look backwards! To fix it, click the word "left" in the turn block and pick "right" instead. Then press play to check. If it still isn't right, try changing 0.25 to 0.5. That makes it a half turn.

Good news, this is easy to fix yourself! In "When the scene starts", your penguin says Hello, turns, then moves. Each block takes about one second, so it all flies by. Most blocks have a duration detail. Click the turn block, open its extra details, and set duration to a bigger number, like 3. Do the same for the move block. For the say block, a bigger duration keeps the bubble up for longer. You can also put a delay block between two blocks, so the penguin waits before doing the next thing. Try one change, then press play to see how it looks!
